sections.causes_of_chikungunya_fever:
It is caused by a virus called alpha virus which is carried by Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, a breed of mosquitoes. The primary reason for spreading this virus is stagnated water where mosquitoes lay their eggs. It commonly occurs in monsoons. 
 Transmission of chikungunya virus 
 It is a highly infectious disease which may transmit from one person to another. If a mosquito bites an infected person then the virus gets into its body and now when this mosquito bites a healthy person then it is transferred to a healthy body. The virus is active only during the daytime.
sections.diagnosis_of_chikungunya_fever:
It is similar to dengue fever. Chikungunya fever is diagnosed on the basis of serological tests like ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assays) for detection of antibodies like IgG and IgM and RT- PCR (Reverse Transcriptase polymerase chain reaction). These tests are used to detect the presence of viruses in blood. 
 Ayurvedic Outlook 
 In ayurveda, it is known as sandhi jwara that literally means ‘fever of the joints’. The symptoms of Sandhijwara and Chikungunya are very similar. There are three basic energies in the body – vata, pitta and kapha which are responsible for healthy life. Imbalance of any three energies results in health complications. Chikungunya fever is considered as vata dosha disorder. Vata is an air component in our body which represents the air which we breathe and gases dissolved in blood. Aggravated vata dosha is responsible for chikungunya fever.

 Ayurveda is an ancient science of life which is helpful in management of various diseased conditions in a natural and healthy way. There is no specific medicine available for this disease but Ayurveda helps to manage the symptoms associated with this disease. There are number of herbs like Giloy (Tinospora cordifolia) , Spirulina (Spirulina platensis) , Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) , Sonth (Zingiber officinale) etc. used in herbal formulations.
